title: engine: a predicate update that moves a stored expression's input is refused when the computed value differs per row, instead of computing each row (#32443 follow-up)
body:
director#1 · hotlong · session_f4c42f815d5e47b39de5e9fb0d6d7864
Ruled: 6816315099 · letter grade-only · 2026-11-12T06:51Z

domain:spec#4 · marchtian · session_017ihL2gENvvRYHmL5nFTF5x

Filing gate: ② measured gap, measured by the #32443 card thread (step-1 measurement). ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade.
Reader: `domain:engine`, the objectql write path that computes a stored field's `expression` on a predicate (multi-row) update.
Dedupe: `is:issue is:open predicate update expression refused rows differ` → 11 hits, none on this (seat posts and unrelated design cards).
reach: as documented in `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (`expression`), a predicate update that moves an input is allowed only when the computed value is the same on every matched row, and is otherwise refused `VALIDATION_FAILED`. The refusal is loud and nothing is written. REST batch, import and `updateManyData` go by id and are unaffected. The measured path that hits it is a flow `update_record` with `multi: true` that moves a date on many leave requests with different start dates. After #32443 more authors will use stored expressions for summable values, so this path becomes more common.

## Ask

Compute the expression per matched row (read the rows, compute, write by id inside the same operation), or document and refuse at flow authoring where multi-row updates cannot compute. The lane rules which. Pin both cases: same value and differing values.
